name: Sariska Tiger Camp Restaurant
why_it_matters: 70-room safari-circuit resort just off the Alwar-Jaipur State Highway in Village Dhawala — multi-cuisine dining with an outdoor section. Daily buffet plus a la carte; the closest mid-tier base for Sariska Tiger Reserve.
insider_tip: Buffet dinner is the standard offering; à la carte takes longer and is hit-or-miss on weekdays. Room-service breakfast before the morning safari is the smarter timing.
signature_address: Sariska Tiger Camp Resort, Alwar-Jaipur State Highway, Village Dhawala, Alwar District, Rajasthan 301001

name: RTDC Tiger Den Restaurant
why_it_matters: Rajasthan Tourism (RTDC) lodge sitting at the entrance of Sariska Tiger Reserve — 31 rooms, modest restaurant, well-stocked bar serving scotch, wine and beer. The cheapest sit-down at the gate, used by drivers and budget safari travellers.
insider_tip: The bar stocks better whisky than the restaurant tier suggests — fine for a sundowner before the morning safari but order food from the kitchen, not the bar menu.
signature_address: Hotel Tiger Den (RTDC), near Forest Rest House, Sariska, Alwar District, Rajasthan 301022

name: Sariska Palace Restaurant
why_it_matters: Heritage hotel in a former royal hunting lodge built in 1892 by Maharaja Jai Singh of Alwar to commemorate the visit of the Duke of Connaught — French architect, Rajasthani-French hybrid architecture. 80-seat multi-cuisine restaurant with Rajasthani, Indian, Continental and Chinese sections. 120-acre estate.
insider_tip: It's a non-resident-friendly heritage hotel but the property is large — call for directions to the dining wing rather than guessing once you arrive at the gate.
signature_address: The Sariska Palace, Sariska, Alwar District, Rajasthan 301022
